meta.title: ISP Group LLC (Florida) - US public procurement of water-treatment chemicals: economics & sourcing model
meta.units_note: ton = short ton (2,000 lb) unless stated; 'dry ton' = 100% basis; prices are delivered (FOB destination) municipal bid/award prices unless noted. Hypo 12.5% ~ 9.9-10 lb/gal; caustic 50% ~ 12.76 lb/gal (6.38 lb NaOH/gal); liquid alum ~ 11.1 lb/gal (~5.4 lb dry/gal at 48.5%).
meta.method: Unit prices taken from public bid tabulations / board award memos 2024-2026 (links per row). Where a figure is a conversion or estimate it is flagged in 'note'. Landed-cost and margin figures are model estimates, not quotes.
caveats: Bid prices include delivery to the plant; small-lot (tote/drum) and remote sites price 20-60% above bulk.
Many bids specify unit basis inconsistently (wet ton vs dry ton vs gal vs lb) - always normalize before comparing.
AD/CVD rates for potassium permanganate (China) and calcium hypochlorite (China) are from memory of prior notices - marked verify_required.

logistics.domestic_bulk_truck: Tank truck 4,000-4,500 gal: ~4-7 USD/loaded mile; typical 150-mile delivery 800-1,200 USD/load (estimate).

list.note: Require NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 listing of exact plant

list.verdict: Avoid: 301 (25%) + 12.5% + AD on carbon/cal-hypo/isos; plus truce-expiry risk

NSF_ANSI_CAN_60.required: Required/referenced by 49 states for all direct additives; nearly every bid demands certificate + NSF mark + MUL on label/BOL.
NSF_ANSI_CAN_60.who_holds: Manufacturer, per product per production facility.
NSF_ANSI_CAN_60.can_reseller_use_manufacturer_listing: YES if product is shipped in the ORIGINAL SEALED container/bulk load from the certified facility with the certified company/product name, facility and MUL on label/BOL (drop-ship or sealed warehousing allowed). NO if reseller repackages, dilutes, blends, transfers or relabels off-site - then reseller needs its own NSF 60 distributor certification (annual audit + sample testing).
NSF_ANSI_CAN_60.private_label: 'Another Name For' (ANF) listing: private label applied at the certified plant, via 3-party agreement manufacturer-distributor-NSF; cheapest way to sell under ISP Group brand.
NSF_ANSI_CAN_60.cost_estimate: Own distributor/ANF listing ~5-15k USD initial + ~3-8k/yr per site/product family (estimate; get NSF quote)

AWWA_standards.B701/B702/B703: Sodium fluoride / sodium fluorosilicate / fluorosilicic acid
AWWA_standards.B502-B505: Sodium/zinc/ortho/poly phosphates (B502 sodium polyphosphate, B503 sodium ortho, B505 sodium hexametaphosphate, B506 zinc ortho)
AWWA_standards.practice: Supplier must deliver COA per AWWA spec per load; utilities may test and reject. Get current editions (AWWA store, ~70-120 USD each).

Buy_American.federal_BAA_FAR_25: Applies to direct federal purchases (e.g., military bases, VA, federal parks) - domestic end products; chemicals manufactured in US qualify; imports need exceptions.
Buy_American.BABA_IIJA_2021: Applies to iron/steel, manufactured products and construction materials INCORPORATED into federally funded infrastructure (SRF). Consumable O&M chemicals are generally NOT covered; GAC/filter media in a capital project may be treated as part of the project - check EPA SRF guidance & the specific spec.
Buy_American.AIS: American Iron & Steel for SRF - not relevant to chemicals.
Buy_American.state_local: Florida s.287.084: preference applied against out-of-state bidders whose home state grants preference (reciprocal) - FL-based ISP Group benefits in FL. Many TX/FL cities grant 5% local-vendor preference (e.g., Abilene). Small/minority business programs (FL OSD certification, county SBE) can add points/set-asides.

bonds.bid_bond: Typical 5% of bid value (some use cashier's check).
bonds.performance_bond: Often 100% of annual contract value or a fixed sum (e.g., 10-25k) for chemical supply; many small-city bids require none.
bonds.new_LLC_reality: Surety underwrites owner credit + financials; start-up gets 'credit-based' small-bond program up to ~250-500k at 2-4% premium, often with personal indemnity and possibly collateral. SBA Surety Bond Guarantee program covers contracts up to 9M (14M federal) - helps new firms.
bonds.cost_estimate: Premium 1.5-3% of bonded amount for first 2-3 years.

insurance.general_liability: 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate (standard bid requirement; some FL counties 2M/4M + umbrella 5M)
insurance.auto: 1M CSL standard; carriers hauling bulk hazmat need FMCSA minimum 5M (certain hazmat in bulk, 49 CFR 387.9) or 1M (other placarded hazmat) - if ISP uses third-party carriers, require their COIs and add hired/non-owned auto 1M
insurance.pollution: Contractors/transportation pollution liability 1-5M (often required for bulk chemical deliveries)
insurance.products_liability: Included in GL; confirm no chemical exclusion
insurance.budget: ~15-40k USD/yr for a lean trading LLC with no owned trucks (estimate)

hazmat_DOT.PHMSA_registration: Required for offerors of placarded hazmat (49 CFR 107.601). 2026-27 fee: 275 USD small business / 2,600 others (incl. 25 processing). Electronic only.
hazmat_DOT.training: 49 CFR 172.704 hazmat employee training every 3 years for anyone preparing shipping papers/BOL, incl. ISP staff acting as 'offeror'.
hazmat_DOT.security_plan: 49 CFR 172.800 if offering bulk quantities of certain classes (e.g., chlorine, 5.1 oxidizers like cal-hypo in large lots).
hazmat_DOT.FMCSA_HMSP: Hazmat Safety Permit only for TIH (chlorine, SO2, anhydrous ammonia) etc. - avoid these products.
hazmat_DOT.carrier_vetting: Use carriers with USDOT/MC authority, satisfactory safety rating, hazmat endorsement drivers, tank-wash certificates (food/NSF-grade dedicated trailers for potable chemicals).

compliance.EPA_TSCA_import: Importer must certify TSCA compliance on each chemical import (positive certification; 19 CFR 12.118-12.127, 40 CFR 707 Subpart B) - substances must be on TSCA Inventory (all listed commodities are). Mixtures/blends: verify every component.
compliance.EPA_FIFRA: Hypochlorites, cal-hypo tablets, chlorine, copper sulfate (algaecide claims) and some disinfectants are pesticides: product must be EPA-registered, producing establishment registered, and importer files EPA Notice of Arrival (Form 3540-1) before entry; state pesticide registration (FL FDACS) to sell.
compliance.OSHA_SDS_GHS: SDS (GHS rev.) for each product, English labels; SDS submitted with bids.
compliance.EPCRA_Tier_II: If storing >= threshold (10,000 lb or EHS TPQ) at a FL warehouse - Tier II report to FDEM by 1 Mar.
compliance.CBP: Importer of record number, continuous bond, licensed customs broker; ISF (10+2) for ocean.
compliance.FL_registration: Sunbiz LLC active, FEIN, W-9, FL sales-tax exemption certificates from public buyers, vendor registration (MyFloridaMarketPlace, DemandStar, BidNet, Bonfire, OpenGov, PlanetBids, VendorLink).

recommendation.verdict: Enter as a lean 'bid-trader + spec specialist' focused on SE (FL/GA/AL/SC) and TX small-to-mid utilities, buying domestically NSF-60-listed products shipped in original sealed packaging (drop-ship), and importing ONLY high-value/low-freight solids (coconut GAC/PAC, KMnO4) from India/Sri Lanka/Philippines with NSF-60-listed mills. Avoid bulk commodity liquids and anything China-origin.

go_to_market_steps: 1. Register on FL/GA/TX bid portals (DemandStar, BidNet, Bonfire, OpenGov, PlanetBids, MyFloridaMarketPlace); scrape awards for target products; build price database from tabs like those cited.

2. Sign distributor/reseller agreements with: Carus (permanganate, phosphates), a carbon producer/importer (Jacobi, Carbon Activated, Haycarb) or Indian NSF-listed mill; a toll blender for ortho blends with NSF 60 ANF private label; SNF/Kemira/Solenis secondary distributor for polymers.
3. Bid only items where ISP cost <= 80% of last award; prefer small/medium utilities with 1-3 bidders and 'or equal' specs.
4. Keep everything drop-shipped in sealed original packaging (preserves NSF 60 without own certification). Use vetted hazmat carriers; ISP registers with PHMSA ($275) and trains staff.
5. Line up surety (credit-based bond program / SBA SBG) and insurance (GL 1M/2M, umbrella 2-5M, HNOA auto 1M, pollution 1-2M) before first bid.
6. Pilot import: one 40HC of coconut GAC/PAC from an NSF-60-listed Indian/Sri Lankan mill into Port Everglades/JAX; sell to 3-5 FL/GA utilities; validate jar tests.
7. Avoid China-origin anything until US-China truce is formalized; even then 301 (25%) + 12.5% + AD make it uncompetitive.
key_risks: Manufacturer refusing to supply a reseller that bids against it
Section 301 forced-labor rate changes / new 232 or 301 actions
Liability for off-spec delivery (penalties, replacement cost)
Payment terms vs import prepayment (working capital)
